These include: A blood test and an ultrasound test during the first trimester of pregnancy. This is the most accepted approach for screening during the first trimester. A blood test enables a health care provider to check for "markers," such as certain proteins, in the mother's blood that suggest an increased likelihood of Down syndrome. 2 Then the health care provider does an ultrasound test, which uses high-frequency sound waves to create images.
